verdict: Avoid new unsecured namkeen exposure in Indore; lend only to established, compliant units with assessed raw-material pass-through and tight monthly stock-and-GST discipline.
title: Indore snacks & namkeen: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Namkeen and sweets is a daily-conversion business: buy besan, potato, milk, sugar, edible oil and dry fruit, fry and pack, sell through own counters and distributors, collect cash.** Value sits in the brand and the counter location, not the plant; cash sits in finished stock and festive receivables. Indore pricing shows the cost pass-through problem plainly: namkeen moved to ₹300-350 per kg from ₹240-260, kaju katli to ₹1,100-1,200 per kg from ₹900, khoya sweets to ₹600-650 per kg from ₹500, and a sweet box now costs ₹18 against ₹12 [3]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit actually re-priced its SKUs this season; if it absorbed costs silently, ask for the gross-margin trend by month.

## What has changed now
**The local signal is weak: Madhya Pradesh GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 6.2 pp slower [D].** Nationally, bank credit is running +25.3% YoY against output +5.1%, a 20.2 pp gap [D] — money is chasing this trade faster than demand is growing. Locally, food safety inspectors covered 15 shops and drew 54 samples in Indore [1]; treat that as a compliance-cost and licence-risk item, not noise. Peer results are mixed: Prataap grew revenue 20% YoY to INR5b in 1QFY27 with namkeen leading on double-digit volume growth [5], while Gopal Snacks grew revenue only 1.8% YoY to ₹400.8 crore in Q3 FY26 though EBITDA nearly doubled to ₹30.4 crore at 7.6% margin [6]. Rating commentary flags the core risk: passing on raw-material increases is hard amid intense competition where brand presence is moderate and packs are small [10].

## Where to grow
**Pursue Indore units with own retail counters plus a distributor base, clean FSSAI paperwork, and a demonstrated festive re-pricing.** Gopal targets ₹1,800-1,900 crore FY27 revenue at 8-9% EBITDA margin [7] — that is the scale benchmark for organised players, not for your borrower. Avoid unbranded job-work fryers selling loose namkeen to wholesale, and avoid anyone whose entire festive season is funded by us. Sources say little specific about Indore's unit economics; lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending, not balance-sheet lending: stock statement plus receivables ageing monthly, GST returns every month, and a drawing power capped on paid stock.** Take monthly stock-and-book-debt statements, quarterly FSSAI licence and inspection status, and a covenant that any SKU price change is reported. Rating work notes working capital is inherently low because food is perishable and restaurant sales are cash [9] — so if your borrower's inventory days are high, ask why. For forays into new geographies, ICRA flags execution and taste-acceptability risk [8]; keep expansion funding out of the core limit.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch stock build-up ahead of Diwali, discount-led sales, and any gap between GST turnover and bank credits.** If namkeen realisations fall back toward ₹240-260 per kg [3] while input costs stay high, the unit is buying volume — cut limits. If a sample failure or licence notice appears [1], freeze fresh disbursal until resolved.
